name: Valentin Borisovich Aleskovskii
summary: Chemist by education, graduate of the Leningrad Technological Institute by Lensovet; author of the 'framework' hypothesis and co-founder, with his student S. I. Kol'tsov, of the molecular layering (ML) method. Organizer and permanent head of the scientific school 'Chemistry of highly organized substances'; author of over 450 scientific publications including 12 books and monographs and more than 150 inventions.

name: Stanislav Ivanovich Kol'tsov
summary: Chemical engineer, graduate student and lifelong collaborator of V. B. Aleskovskii at the LTI by Lensovet; co-inventor of the molecular layering method, whose doctoral dissertation laid out the key principles of ML and introduced the term 'chemical assembly'.

name: T. Suntola
summary: Finnish physicist by education, inventor of atomic layer epitaxy (ALE), holder of the first Finnish patents on the method, whose work led to industrial production of electroluminescent displays.

name: Anatolii A. Malygin
summary: Student of Aleskovskii and Kol'tsov; professor and head of the Department of Chemical Nanotechnology and Electronics Engineering Materials at St. Petersburg State Technological Institute; lead author of the essay.

name: Victor E. Drozd
summary: Physicist, graduate of the Leningrad Electrotechnical Institute, one of the few physicists in the ML group; builder of the first manually controlled vacuum ML reactor and later automated vacuum ML equipment; at St. Petersburg State University, Department of Solid State Chemistry.

name: Vladimir M. Smirnov
summary: Student of Aleskovskii and Kol'tsov; professor at St. Petersburg State University, Department of Solid State Chemistry; first to describe the 'monolayer effect' in ML-synthesized oxide monolayers.

name: Anatolii A. Malkov
summary: Student of Aleskovskii and Kol'tsov at LTI by Lensovet; researcher at St. Petersburg State Technological Institute and main developer of nanodoped blends for ceramic insulators.

name: G. N. Kuznetsova
summary: Graduate student at LTI by Lensovet advised by V. B. Aleskovskii and A. M. Shevyakov; her candidate thesis on IR spectroscopy of hydrated silica adopted Kol'tsov's method.

name: A. N. Volkova
summary: Student of Aleskovskii and Kol'tsov at LTI by Lensovet whose candidate thesis dealt with molecular layering reactions of chlorides with silica gel.

name: G. V. Sveshnikova
summary: Student jointly mentored by Kol'tsov and Aleskovskii; studied thin oxide layers on silicon surfaces by ML, including ellipsometry of TiO2/SiO2 nanolaminates.

name: Augusta Petrovna Dushina
summary: Graduate student of V. B. Aleskovskii who developed the method of destructive-epitaxial transformations (DET) for modifying the core atoms of solids.

name: A. M. Shevyakov
summary: Specialist in infrared spectroscopy at LTI by Lensovet, co-advisor of G. N. Kuznetsova and student of Aleskovskii.

name: Riikka Puurunen
summary: Senior Scientist at VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland; co-initiator of the Virtual Project on the History of ALD and author of reviews and an essay on the history of ALD in Finland.

name: Jonas Sundqvist
summary: Group Leader High-k Devices at Fraunhofer IPMS-CNT, Germany; co-initiator of the Virtual Project on the History of ALD.

name: Aziz Abdulagatov
summary: Postdoctoral Fellow at NIST Boulder, USA; co-initiator of the Virtual Project on the History of ALD and assisted in creating an ALD group at Dagestan State University.

name: N. A. Kosygin
summary: Prime Minister of the USSR who became interested in molecular layering and ordered the establishment of a committee on the subject.

name: E. K. Kalinin
summary: Deputy Minister of Education who proposed an inter-university program under Aleskovskii's supervision as a compromise to the proposed Institute of Chemical Assembly of Materials.

name: D. Damyanov
summary: Bulgarian scientist from the Burgas Institute of Technology engaged in ML studies of catalysts.

name: V. N. Pak
summary: Ph.D. student of Aleskovskii; author of the first ML doctoral thesis after Kol'tsov's, on quantum-chemical studies of oxide coatings; later supervisor at St. Petersburg State Pedagogical University.

name: V. F. Dergachev
summary: Researcher who developed an automated multi-sectional fluidized-bed ML apparatus for powder coating used to produce the IVS-1 indicator.

name: O. K. Sulimov
summary: Co-author with Aleskovskii of a Russian patent related to chemical-informational synthesis.

name: Emperor Nicholas I
summary: Russian emperor whose decree established the practical institute of technology in Leningrad (St. Petersburg).

name: L. Niinisto
summary: Finnish ALE scientist who supported the presentation of the first Soviet ML report at the 1st International Symposium on Atomic Layer Epitaxy.

name: M. Pessa
summary: Professor who provided information enabling V. E. Drozd's first ML report at the ALE symposium.

name: Mary
summary: City in Turkmenistan, birthplace of V. B. Aleskovskii.

name: Proletarskaya station, Rostov region
summary: Station in the Rostov region of the USSR, birthplace of S. I. Kol'tsov.

name: Leningrad
summary: City in Russia (USSR), home of the LTI by Lensovet and Leningrad State University.

name: Espoo/Helsinki
summary: Finnish capital region, site of the 1st International Symposium on Atomic Layer Epitaxy and the 12th Baltic ALD conference.

name: Kyoto
summary: Japanese city, site of the AVS 14th International Conference on Atomic Layer Deposition.

name: Leningrad Technological Institute by Lensovet
aliases: St. Petersburg State Technological Institute (Technical University)
summary: Oldest chemical engineering institute in Russia, established as a 'practical institute of technology'; the institute where Aleskovskii and Kol'tsov created and experimentally substantiated the molecular layering method.

name: Naval Research Institute in Leningrad
summary: Research institute in Leningrad where Aleskovskii worked as a research fellow after graduating.

name: Leningrad State University
summary: Classical university in Leningrad/St. Petersburg where Aleskovskii served as rector and organized the Department of Solid State Chemistry.

name: Department of Analytical Chemistry, LTI by Lensovet
summary: Department at LTI by Lensovet headed by Aleskovskii where Kol'tsov enrolled as a graduate student.

name: Department of Chemistry of Solids, LTI by Lensovet
aliases: Solid State Chemistry Department at LTI by Lensovet
Department of Chemical Engineering of Materials and Electronics Products
Department of Chemical Nanotechnology and Electronics Engineering Materials
summary: One of the first departments of chemistry of solids in the USSR, founded and first chaired by Aleskovskii at LTI by Lensovet; home of the molecular layering research group.

name: Department of Solid State Chemistry, Leningrad State University
summary: Department at Leningrad (St. Petersburg) State University organized and supervised by Aleskovskii, where ML research continues under his and Kol'tsov's students.

name: Academy of Sciences of the USSR
summary: Soviet national academy of sciences, of which Aleskovskii was a corresponding member.

name: Scientific school 'Chemistry of highly organized substances'
summary: Leading Soviet/Russian scientific school organized and permanently headed by V. B. Aleskovskii, which regularly held international and Russian conferences.

name: 'Chemical assembly of materials' inter-university program
summary: Inter-university scientific and technical program headed by Aleskovskii and led by LSU and LTI by Lensovet, founded by the Ministry of Higher Education of the RSFSR.

name: Ministry of Higher Education of the RSFSR
summary: Ministry of the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic that founded the 'Chemical assembly of materials' inter-university program.

name: Svetlana
summary: One of the leading USSR electronics engineering organizations, partner in demonstrating ML-made dielectric thin films for MOS structures and later in ceramic insulators for X-ray tubes.

name: Burgas Institute of Technology
summary: Bulgarian institute where D. Damyanov worked and defended his doctoral dissertation on ML.

name: Virtual Project on the History of ALD
summary: International project in which early Russian ML publications were presented and discussed by more than 30 scientists from 10 countries.

name: Leningrad Scientific Center of the USSR Academy of Sciences
summary: Regional center of the USSR Academy of Sciences, of which Aleskovskii was one of the leading organizers; currently headed by Nobel laureate Zhores I. Alferov.

name: Council of Rectors of Leningrad
summary: Body of Leningrad university rectors chaired for many years by Aleskovskii.

name: Supreme Soviet of the Russian Federation (SFSR)
summary: Legislature of the RSFSR, in which Aleskovskii served as a member and headed Commissions on Education, Youth and others.

name: Pravda
summary: Leading Soviet newspaper.

name: Leningrad Electrotechnical Institute
summary: Institute from which V. E. Drozd graduated before joining the ML group.

name: 'Framework' hypothesis
summary: Solid-state concept proposed by Aleskovskii according to which the chemical structure of any solid contains a 'core' (superpolyatomic radical) surrounded by surface functional groups; solids are treated as gigantic molecules ('supramolecules') obeying classical chemistry, opening two routes of transformation (surface functional groups or core).

name: Molecular layering method
summary: Method of sequentially building monolayers of structural units with given composition on a solid surface by irreversible, alternating gas-phase reactions with surface functional groups; the Soviet counterpart of ALD/ALE.

name: Framework hypothesis and experience the preparation of certain active catalysts
summary: Doctoral dissertation of V. B. Aleskovskii at LTI by Lensovet in which the 'framework' hypothesis was originally formulated.

name: Active silica
summary: Candidate of chemical sciences thesis of V. B. Aleskovskii.

name: Silica Gel: Its Structure and Chemical Properties
summary: Monograph by S. I. Kol'tsov and V. B. Aleskovskii (Goskhimizdat, Leningrad) based on Kol'tsov's candidate work, serving as a basis for subsequent ML research.

name: The study of interaction of carbon tetrachloride with silica gel
summary: Candidate dissertation of S. I. Kol'tsov at LTI by Lensovet, in which molecular layering at atmospheric pressure was reported, including a diagram of the first flow-type ML setup.

name: Synthesis of solids by the Molecular Layering Method
summary: Doctoral dissertation of S. I. Kol'tsov (383 pp., LTI by Lensovet) defining the ML method, formulating its principles, classifying ML reactions and introducing the term 'chemical assembly'.

name: The principles of synthesis of solids (patent application № 1642785/23-26)
summary: Patent application by Aleskovskii and Kol'tsov attempting to patent the ML process; declined by the patent office.

name: US 4 058 430 (atomic layer epitaxy patent)
summary: First patent of T. Suntola and J. Antson on thin-film deposition named 'atomic layer epitaxy (ALE)', describing alternate deposition of thin monolayers under high vacuum using elemental precursors.

name: US 4 413 022 / FIN 57975 (zinc sulfide ALE patent)
summary: Patent by T. Suntola, A. Pakkala and S. Lindfors on zinc sulfide film deposition by ALE using alternating doses of zinc chloride and hydrogen sulfide molecular precursors on glass.

name: The stoichiometry and synthesis of solid compounds
aliases: Stoichiometry and Synthesis of Solid Compounds
summary: Monograph by V. B. Aleskovskii (Nauka, Leningrad, 142 pp.) analyzing the history of solid-state chemistry and presenting the framework hypothesis and supramolecular chemistry of compounds.

name: Chemistry of solids
summary: Textbook for high schools by V. B. Aleskovskii (Higher School, Moscow, 256 pp.), prepared on the basis of his stoichiometry monograph.

name: Chemistry of supramolecular compounds
summary: Monograph by V. B. Aleskovskii (St. Petersburg University Publishing House, 253 pp.) based on his lecture course on the chemistry of supramolecular compounds.

name: Chemical-informational synthesis
aliases: Chemical and information synthesis. The beginnings of the theory. Methods
summary: Last released textbook by V. B. Aleskovskii (St. Petersburg University Publishing House, 72 pp.), part of the new concept of the chemistry of highly organized substances.

name: Method of destructive-epitaxial transformations (DET)
summary: Method developed by A. P. Dushina for transforming the 'core' of a solid by substitution of bulk atoms, typically by adding the solid to a liquid reactant.

name: IVS-1 sorbent-indicator
summary: Silica gel with a vanadium oxide monolayer produced by ML, used industrially as a high-sensitivity gas-phase humidity indicator.

name: FS-1-3 sorbent
summary: Silica gel modified with phosphorus oxide layers by ML, an industrial sorbent for water vapor, amines and organic compounds.

name: Vacuum ML reactor combined with an ellipsometer
summary: First ML system with in situ film thickness monitoring during deposition on polished silicon, combining an ellipsometer and a Peltier element, built by V. E. Drozd.

name: Patent Rus. 2172731
summary: Russian patent by V. B. Aleskovskii and O. K. Sulimov associated with the theory of quantum chemical technologies and synthesis of nano-sized active carbon.

name: Pravda article on chemical assembly
summary: Article by V. B. Aleskovskii on chemical assembly in the newspaper Pravda that drew the interest of Prime Minister N. A. Kosygin.
